messages:
anna_support: Hi — escalating from support intake. Customer can't resolve internal svc `payments.internal` and their API returns 502s. They started after an on-prem peering change.

customer_bob: repro from their side: `dig +short payments.internal` returns nothing; full dig shows NXDOMAIN. App logs show `GET /v1/payments` -> upstream connect error.

miguel_eng: thanks. Can you paste VPC id and whether you recently added an inbound/outbound Route53 Resolver rule? Also any DNS forwarders on-prem?

customer_bob: VPC vpc-0c1234ab, yes we recently added a resolver forward rule for `corp.internal` to point at on-prem resolvers for hybrid services. We didn't expect `payments.internal` to be affected.

anna_support: can you run this from one of the app instances?

```
# from app instance
dig @10.0.0.2 payments.internal +trace
```

customer_bob: output: `;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345` and trace shows query forwarded to on-prem DNS 10.200.0.5 which returns NXDOMAIN.

tony_sre: aha — likely a Route53 Resolver rule for `.` or a too-broad domain that matches `payments.internal` got associated to the VPC. That will forward queries to on-prem and override Route53 private hosted zone answers.

miguel_eng: pls run:
```
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=CreatorRequestId,Values=*
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0c1234ab
```

customer_bob: ran both. Associations show `rslvr-0123456789` associated to vpc-0c1234ab; resolver rule domain is `internal` and target IPs include 10.200.0.5.

tony_sre: confirm: there is also a private hosted zone called `internal` with `payments` A record in Route53? If so, it usually wins, but if resolver rule is more specific or misconfigured it can forward and shadow answers.

customer_bob: there is a private hosted zone `internal` in AWS account A with correct records, but the forwarder was intended for `corp.internal` only. Looks like rule domain was `internal` accidentally.

anna_support: next steps: (1) disassociate the resolver rule from the VPC (`aws route53resolver disassociate-resolver-rule --association-id rslvrassoc-...`), (2) fix the rule to `corp.internal` and re-associate only where needed, (3) flush node caches / restart app DNS resolver.

customer_bob: disassociated and flushed cache. `dig +short payments.internal` now returns `10.10.5.12`. App 200s restored. Thanks!

miguel_eng: adding runbook note: validate new resolver rules do not use overly-broad domain names; we should add an alert when a FORWARD resolver rule is associated to a customer VPC for domains that overlap AWS private zones.

anna_support: following up in case of regression; customer confirmed stability. Closing ticket but leaving as internal action for infra automation. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: note: created infra-issue #INFRA-221 to add pre-association checks.
